correctness.rationale: The exact binomial-harmonic formula is the derivative of a rising factorial divided by n!, with integer polynomial derivative. Fourteen fully specified prime-power congruences are independently evaluated by integer arithmetic, their moduli multiply to 45!, and the explicit Chinese-remainder residue simultaneously satisfies all. Polynomial periodicity proves the infinite progression, not finite extrapolation. The first possible odd non-prime-power nonsquarefree integer is 3^2*5=45, and the published even/prime-power nonintegrality theorem excludes all lower indices. Direct rational evaluations at three distinct certified orders provide a separate check.

value.rationale: The first nonsquarefree index admitting an integer hyperharmonic is a natural sharp boundary in an index-property classification: below it a published structural obstruction excludes all squareful n, while a concrete CRT theorem opens an infinite positive-density order class exactly at n=45. It distinguishes the previously known squarefree 33/39 positive examples from the first squareful case. The exact arithmetic certificate solves a motivated presence/absence question; the result is not merely verification that arbitrary isolated large numbers are integral.
